title: Priority mapping and skip-level asks (Q3) - draft v0.1
body:
Purpose:
This note is a compact working draft for mapping top-line priorities for Q3, aligning proposed OKRs across org pillars, and coordinating the skip-level meeting agenda that will feed into the company all-hands. It's intentionally short and focused on decisions we need from Exec + people leads by July 11.

Context / What motivated this: 
- We have strong signals from product telemetry and customer conversations that cost-per-inference and latency tail spikes are the two engineering risk areas.
- Sales and CS flag Dedicated contracts ramping in Q3 requiring predictable SLA language and capacity commitments.
- Recruiting cadence is slower than plan; leadership wants clarity on which hires are must-dos vs nice-to-have.

Goals for this doc:
1) Propose 3 prioritized company-level initiatives mapped to measurable outcomes (OKR-style).
2) Surface skip-level discussion prompts to validate tradeoffs with ICs and managers.
3) Define one consolidated run-of-show for an all-hands that communicates decisions and next steps.

Proposed top-line priorities (draft) - ranked by near-term impact and cross-functional dependency:
A. Predictable inference economics (Cost SLOs + telemetry)
  - Why: Customer commitments require a predictable unit-economics story; internal ops needs clearer cost signals to avoid over-provisioning.
  - Candidate OKR (K1): Reduce 95th-percentile per-token cost by 18% for hosted API traffic measured at model-route granularity by end of Q3.
  - Candidate OKR (K2): Ship token-level cost telemetry to Console (per-route) with 7-day retention and alerting on +10% week-over-week spikes.
  - Key owners: Product-hosted-api (lead: Lila Gomez), Engineering-runtime (lead: Marcus Chen), Finance (Priya Singh).
  - Major dependencies: Optimize batching defaults, billing pipeline changes, and dashboarding work.

B. SLA & capacity operationalization for Dedicated customers
  - Why: Several pilots expect contractual SLAs and predictable latency/throughput.
  - Candidate OKR (K1): Define and publish Dedicated SLO SLA tiers and runbook; pilot with 2 customers by end of Q3.
  - Candidate OKR (K2): Automate capacity reservation workflow so Dedicated customers get committed baseline throughput within 24hrs of an approved change request.
  - Owners: Product-dedicated (owner: Ethan Brooks), Infra (owner: Marcus Chen), Solutions Eng.
  - Major dependencies: Capacity accounting, telemetry for utilization, legal review for SLA wording.

C. Developer productivity and onboarding (reduce iteration friction)
  - Why: Faster dev iteration reduces time-to-ship for prioritized infra and product improvements.
  - Candidate OKR (K1): Reduce median dev feedback loop (local->integration) from 2 hours to 30 minutes for common testcases used by platform and runtime teams.
  - Candidate OKR (K2): Deliver a self-guided Dedicated onboarding template (VPC & non-VPC) that reduces solutions eng touch time by 30%.
  - Owners: Developer-experience, Console-and-tooling.

Tradeoffs we expect to discuss:
- Investing in cost telemetry and billing may delay feature work for Dedicated SLA polish.
- Aggressively optimizing batching/quantization risks quality regressions; we need guardrails (evals + rollback).
- Headcount: prioritize infra/runtime hires vs solutions and sales; missing infra hires increases operational risk.

Skip-level plan (how we’ll validate with ICs and managers)
- Timing: Week of July 7th - 10th.
- Format: 45 minute sessions, small cohorts (6–8 people) + one manager optional. Mix of SREs, runtime engineers, product managers, and solutions engineers.
- Objective: Surface execution risks, blockers, and alternative ideas. Capture decisions that will flow to the all-hands.
- Suggested prompts (short):
  1. If we prioritize "predictable inference economics" what would you stop doing to free up time?
  2. What are the top three unknowns that would make the Dedicated SLA work harder to deliver?
  3. For developer productivity, where do you spend the most time waiting on infra or tooling?
  4. What automation or dashboard would change your day-to-day the most?

Logistics for skip-levels:
- Coordinator: Priya Singh (finance) + Ethan Brooks (product-dedicated) to book cohort slots.
- Report-out: each session owner to fill short template (Top-3 takeaways, 2 proposed countermeasures, decisions requested). Collated by July 14.

All-hands / Exec brief run-of-show (single slide per segment, 30–40 minute total)
- 0:00–0:03: Opening (CEO) - state of the company and high-level asks.
- 0:03–0:12: Priorities announced (A/B/C above) with one-sentence outcome and owner.
- 0:12–0:22: Concrete commitments and quick examples (telemetry screenshot, SLA bullet list, onboarding checklist).
- 0:22–0:30: What we are deprioritizing and why (explicit tradeoffs).
- 0:30–0:36: Skip-level findings summary (3 key signals + recommended decisions).
- 0:36–0:40: Clear next steps, owners, and how to follow up (weekly check-ins, dashboard links).

Comms plan (post-all-hands)
- 24h post: single-thread Slack summary + linked document with Q&A.
- 48–72h: Team leads publish team-specific impact notes and updated JIRA tickets for scoping.
- Channels: #company-announcements, #eng-runtime, product updates on Confluence page above.

Decision points for Execs (need responses by Friday, July 11):
1) Validate the three top-line priorities as company-level OKRs for Q3 (A/B/C).
2) Confirm commitment to fund up to 2 infra/runtime hires in Q3 if hiring pipeline continues to lag.
3) Approve skip-level question set (no more than 4 prompts) and allocate 3 hours of each exec’s calendar for skip-levels next week.

Risks and mitigation (short):
- Risk: Over-ambitious scope across three big initiatives -> Mitigation: Hard limit on team-level OKR count; recommend max 1 large cross-org project per eng pod.
- Risk: Telemetry rollout introduces false positives and noise -> Mitigation: Shadow alerts, 2-week quiet window, and an on-call owner to tune thresholds.
- Risk: SLA language legal exposure -> Mitigation: Template SLA with limited financial exposure for Q3 pilots; legal review on ticket ENG-4301.

Appendix: measurement ideas and quick metrics to track
- Cost-per-token bucketed by model family and route (weekly aggregate + P95).
- Dedicated customer tail latency (95th, 99th) per instance type.
- Dev iteration time (median build->integration test time) measured from CI timing tags.

Next steps / owners (by July 14):
- Lila: Draft telemetry dashboard spec and a small mock to present at all-hands.
- Marcus: Start a small pilot to validate batching defaults on one low-risk route; sample results by July 10.
- Ethan: Draft Dedicated SLA pilot plan and customer outreach email template.
- Priya: Prepare quick headcount scenarios (costed) for 0/1/2 infra hires.
- Ava (owner of this doc): Collate skip-level reports and produce a 2-slide summary for the all-hands.

Open questions (for execs to answer in decision doc):
- Are we comfortable with 18% per-token cost target as an aspirational company-level key result, or should we size it to 10–12% to increase probability?
- Which exec is the final arbiter if tradeoffs between Dedicated SLAs and cost telemetry require reallocation of engineering resources mid-quarter?

Notes to reviewers:
- This is a working draft; please add inline comments in Drive or ping me directly. We will consolidate inputs and prepare the final all-hands script Monday July 14.
